# Fall in Gaston County: A Local's Guide to Belmont and Cramerton


Things to do in Belmont and Cramerton, NC


Tri Pointe Homes


•


September 19, 2026


Share this article


Fall along the South Fork Catawba moves at its own pace. The days shorten, the river cools, and two small towns a few minutes apart start pulling out their best seasonal traditions. If you're new to Belmont or Cramerton or just looking for a reason to get outside this season, here's where locals are actually headed.


## **See Daniel Stowe Botanical Garden Turn to Autumn**


Spring gets the tulips and summer gets the daylilies but fall belongs to the ornamental grasses and the late-season color that fills the Four Seasons Garden. The Conservatory stays warm and green no matter what the weather does outside, which makes it an easy stop on a cooler afternoon. Walk the Canal Garden's reflecting pools, follow the Woodland Trail if you'd rather be under trees than beside fountains, and let the kids loose in Lost Hollow, the garden's dedicated children's area.


The garden sits just minutes from[Seven Oaks](https://www.tripointehomes.com/nc/charlotte/seven-oaks) , close enough that a weekday evening walk through the grounds is realistic, not just a weekend plan. Current hours and seasonal programming are posted on their[website](https://www.tripointehomes.com/blog/danielstoweconservancy.org) .


Time it right and you'll catch Village Fall Fest, Saturday, September 26, 2026 from 2 p.m. to 7 p.m. at The Village, free to attend. The Farmhouse Garden Center runs its fall plant sale, local vendors set up with specialty goods, food trucks handle dinner, and the music runs from an afternoon Pickin' on the Porch set into an evening concert from NC musician David Childers.[Details](https://danielstoweconservancy.org/event/village-fall-fest/)


## **Spend an Afternoon in Downtown Belmont**


Stowe Park sits at the center of it, and fall is when downtown Belmont leans into it — string lights, local shops staying open a little later, and a steady rotation of community events through the season. It's a walkable stretch, which makes it a good afternoon even without a specific event on the calendar.


A few stops worth building the walk around:


-


**Nellie's Southern Kitchen** — Southern comfort food from the Jonas family (yes, that Jonas family — Kevin Jonas Sr. named it for his grandmother), and one of the few Main Street stops with a genuine national following.


-


**The Everyday Market** — a café and market with a European lean, good for coffee and something baked that morning before the rest of the walk.


-


**The Collective** — “A mother & daughter ran boutique blending consignment and curated fashions with gifts, home accents, florals and permanent jewelry”


Lauren, one of Tri Pointe's New Home Specialists, lives in Belmont herself and put it best:


> *"Fall is one of my favorite times in Belmont because you can easily grab a coffee and stroll along Main Street, and be surrounded by so much history and natural beauty within minutes. I love that Belmont has this small-town, everyone-knows-everyone feel, with places like Stowe Park (Tally's favorite spot* 🐾 *), Daniel Stowe Conservancy and the river nearby — it really is hard to beat the combination of community, charm and the outdoors that Gaston County has to offer and yet still be so close to the big city."*
>
>
> *— Lauren, New Home Specialist at Tri Pointe Homes and Belmont resident*


**


Downtown also throws BooFest, a Halloween festival with carnival rides, costume contests, trick-or-treating through the festival grounds, and a lineup of Halloween-themed craft vendors. This year it's **Saturday, October 24, 2026, from 2 p.m. to 7 p.m., at Stowe Park (24 S. Main St).**[More Details](https://www.tripointehomes.com/blog/downtownbelmont.org/boofest)


## **Cramerton's Fall Festival Brings the Whole Town Out**


Cramerton's Fall Festival is free, and exactly as small-town as it sounds — games, trick-or-treating, a cakewalk, and a costume contest that kicks off at 5 p.m. Kids get free wristbands for unlimited gameplay, and there's a craft vendor marketplace for the adults browsing while the kids run the games.


This year's festival is **Saturday, October 17, 2026, from 4 p.m. to 7 p.m.** , on the ballfields behind the C.B. Huss Recreation Complex at 8 Julian Street.[Full details](https://www.tripointehomes.com/blog/cramerton.org)


It's an easy trip from[Millstone](https://www.tripointehomes.com/nc/charlotte/millstone) , and it's the sort of event where you run into neighbors more than strangers.


## **Walk, Paddle, or Aim for a Turkey on Goat Island**


Goat Island is 30 acres in the middle of Cramerton, wrapped by the South Fork Catawba, and it works just as well for a slow walk as it does for an active afternoon. There's a tree-house-style playground for kids, walking trails for everyone else, and river access for fishing, kayaking, or canoeing if the water's calling more than the trail is.


Late fall adds a reason to time the visit around an event: the **Turkey Shoot** , Saturday, November 7, 2026, from 10 AM to 12 p.m. at Goat Island Park. It's a bullseye-target shooting challenge with a frozen Thanksgiving turkey on the line — first shot free, then $2 for three shots or $5 for eight, two-turkey limit per person. Open to all ages.[Details](https://www.tripointehomes.com/blog/cramerton.org.) .


It's a short trip from Millstone, and honestly, an easy habit to fall into once the weather turns.


## **Flannel, Fire Pits, and a Fleetwood Mac Tribute at Flannel Fest**


Downtown Cramerton closes out the season with Flannel Fest on **Saturday, November 21, 2026, from 5 p.m. to 9 p.m** . Live music comes from Landslide, a Fleetwood Mac tribute band, alongside food trucks, a mechanical bull, axe throwing, and fire pits with s'mores. There's a flannel awards contest at 6:50 p.m. with categories for best flannel, best pet outfit, and future flannel fan, so bring the dog if it owns a flannel.[Full details.](https://www.tripointehomes.com/blog/cramerton.org)


## **Fall Is a Good Time to See These Neighborhoods for Yourself**


Seven Oaks and Millstone by Tri Pointe Homes® were built close enough to everything in this guide that “close by” isn't a marketing line, it's a walk or a short drive.


[Seven Oaks](https://www.tripointehomes.com/nc/charlotte/seven-oaks) , in Belmont, is a collection of 100 townhomes inside the McLean community, priced from the $400s with three- to five-bedroom floorplans running 1,982 to 2,433 square feet. It sits close enough to Lake Wylie and Daniel Stowe Botanical Garden that a fall evening walk through the garden is a realistic after-work plan, and the McLean trail network starts right outside the door.[Schedule a visit at Seven Oaks today](https://www.tripointehomes.com/nc/charlotte/seven-oaks/#tour-form)


At Millstone, mornings start with the Catawba just past the treeline and evenings end a short walk from downtown Cramerton. Three-bedroom townhomes run 1,850 to 2,024 square feet, priced from the mid $300s.[Schedule a visit today](https://www.tripointehomes.com/nc/charlotte/millstone/#tour-form)


If you're curious what either neighborhood looks like this time of year, fall is a good season to come see it in person.
